what_changed.headline: Global rates and rate volatility intensified; long-end yields reached cycle highs.
what_changed.significance: Tighter financial conditions raise duration and equity-risk sensitivity, although this is source-reported market data rather than independent confirmation.
what_changed.transmission: Higher real and nominal yields support the dollar, pressure duration and precious metals, and increase refinancing costs.

what_changed.headline: US–China trade truce was extended, but core disputes remain unresolved.
what_changed.significance: Near-term escalation risk was reduced without a durable resolution on tariffs, rare earths, AI chips, Taiwan or Iran.
what_changed.transmission: The pause may support sentiment temporarily; unresolved implementation and January expiry preserve geopolitical risk.

what_changed.headline: Physical energy markets remain disrupted despite improved flows.
what_changed.significance: Oil logistics, refining capacity and diesel availability remain vulnerable to geopolitical developments.
what_changed.transmission: Higher fuel costs can lift inflation and weaken fuel-importing currencies and growth-sensitive assets.

executive_decisions.development: Treat duration as the principal cross-asset risk while long-end yields and rate volatility remain elevated.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: Source commentary identifies the bond market as a key risk to equities and reports a sharp rise in Treasury volatility.
executive_decisions.transmission: Higher yields tighten financial conditions, challenge long-duration equities and increase fiscal refinancing pressure.

executive_decisions.development: Keep energy exposure conditional on geopolitical and logistics developments rather than treating higher crude as a settled trend.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: Flows have improved, but physical premiums, refinery outages and geopolitical disruption remain material.
executive_decisions.transmission: A renewed disruption would lift fuel prices and inflation; normalization would reverse part of that pressure.

themes.title: Rates-led tightening versus supply-driven inflation
themes.implication: Bearish for duration and rate-sensitive equities; supportive for the dollar; commodity effects remain differentiated by physical tightness.

themes.title: Managed US–China rivalry
themes.implication: Short-term sentiment support is possible, but durable Chinese-equity or supply-chain re-rating requires implementation evidence.

themes.title: Energy shock versus disinflation
themes.implication: Maintain a bias toward higher front-end and real-rate risk, while recognizing that weaker demand could eventually offset inflation pressure.

themes.title: Resilient investment cycle under tighter discount rates
themes.implication: Favors selective capital-goods and infrastructure exposure over broad duration-sensitive risk.

themes.title: Energy shock meets resilient demand
themes.implication: Prefer caution on duration; the balance remains supportive of USD strength and vulnerable to renewed energy headlines.

themes.title: AI investment remains powerful but increasingly narrow
themes.implication: Broad equity exposure is less compelling than differentiated exposure to infrastructure beneficiaries and disruption risk.

themes.title: Agentic AI and concentration
themes.implication: Selected CPU and infrastructure exposures may benefit, while concentration and valuation-reversal risks remain material.

themes.title: Energy-driven inflation versus growth
themes.implication: Rates retain upside inflation sensitivity while growth-sensitive assets face demand risk; oil can soften tactically without resolving physical tightness.

themes.title: Fiscal credibility and sovereign term premia
themes.implication: French duration and spread exposure remain vulnerable to political or budget setbacks.

themes.title: Energy shock meets policy normalization
themes.implication: Front-end rates remain vulnerable to upside inflation surprises, but weaker real incomes create a later growth downside.

themes.title: AI investment: productivity promise versus concentration risk
themes.implication: AI-linked equities retain a supportive fundamental narrative, while duration and credit are exposed to investment-financing and valuation shocks.

themes.title: Renewed US tightening versus persistent inflation risk
themes.implication: Supports USD and short-end yields; creates a higher hurdle for duration and long-duration equities.

themes.title: Energy shock as the cross-asset policy variable
themes.implication: Persistent energy strength would prolong tightening risk; normalization would reopen disinflation and easing scenarios.

themes.title: AI investment, growth and fiscal crowding-out
themes.implication: Supports selective exposure to durable productivity beneficiaries while cautioning against treating AI as a complete macro or fiscal solution.

themes.title: Energy shock, fiscal supply and the duration premium
themes.implication: The combination is adverse for long-duration rates and rate-sensitive equities, while supporting near-term USD demand; confirmation requires continued energy and yield data.

themes.title: Japan normalization and global duration spillovers
themes.implication: The yen and JGB curve remain sensitive to the balance between faster normalization and fiscal/financial-stability concerns.

themes.title: Energy shock versus policy credibility
themes.implication: Upside risk to front-end and inflation-sensitive rates; downside risk to energy-importing growth assets; dollar support is possible but not assured.

themes.title: AI investment, productivity and financing strain
themes.implication: Supports selective AI infrastructure exposure over the medium term but raises duration, credit and equity-correction risks.
